**RECALL COORDINATION LOG – PRODUCT RECALL 2025-03**

**Log Owner:** Recall Coordination Office, Consumer Product Safety Division
**Log Period:** 10 March 2025 – ongoing
**Time Standard:** Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST, UTC+10) unless noted otherwise. Daylight saving adjustments recorded where applicable.
**Status Codes:** `issued` / `in progress` / `completed`

---

**Entry 001 – 10 March 2025, 09:12 AEST**
**Subject:** Official issue of Product Recall 2025-03

The Recall Coordination Office logged the recall issue date for Product Recall 2025-03 as 2025-03-10. Record status: current. This entry confirms the recall is now formally `issued` and active. All subsequent operational milestones will be recorded against this date.

**Initial directives:**
- Recall notice to be published on the ACCC Product Safety Australia website by 12:00 AEST today.
- Consumer-facing alert to be drafted and circulated to all state and territory consumer affairs offices by close of business.
- Retailer notification pack to be prepared by the Compliance Liaison team (lead: J. Okafor).

**Team assignments (effective immediately):**
| Role | Name | Responsibility |
|------|------|----------------|
| Recall Coordinator | M. Tran | Overall timeline management, milestone tracking |
| Compliance Liaison | J. Okafor | Retailer and supplier notifications |
| Consumer Contact Lead | P. Whitfield | Managing consumer enquiries and refund process |
| Logistics Contact | R. Singh | Return and disposal coordination with warehouses |
| Regulatory Officer | S. Delaney | Liaison with ACCC and state authorities |

**09:45 AEST –** Draft recall notice text received from Regulatory Officer S. Delaney. Sent for legal review. Status: `in progress`.

**10:30 AEST –** Consumer Contact Lead P. Whitfield confirmed the dedicated recall phone line is operational. Hours: 8:30 AM – 6:00 PM AEST, Monday to Friday. Voicemail available outside these hours.

**11:15 AEST –** Logistics Contact R. Singh reported that the initial return authorisation forms (RAFs) are ready for distribution to the three contracted warehouses. Forms will be sent electronically by 2:00 PM.

**12:00 AEST –** Recall notice published on the ACCC Product Safety Australia website. Confirmed by Regulatory Officer S. Delaney. Status: `completed`.

**14:20 AEST –** Retailer notification pack (draft version 1.1) circulated to Compliance Liaison J. Okafor for review. Pack includes: recall summary, product identification guide, refund/replacement procedure, and contact details for the recall line.

**16:45 AEST –** End of day summary. All initial launch activities on track. No exceptions reported.

---

**Entry 002 – 11 March 2025, 08:50 AEST**
**Subject:** Day 2 – Notification and logistics preparation

**08:55 AEST –** Compliance Liaison J. Okafor confirmed that the retailer notification pack (version 1.1) has been approved with minor amendments. Final version to be distributed to all known stockists by 12:00 AEST today.

**09:30 AEST –** Consumer Contact Lead P. Whitfield reported that 47 consumer enquiries were received between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM yesterday. All callers were provided with the recall details and advised to stop using the product immediately.

**10:15 AEST –** Logistics Contact R. Singh confirmed that the three contracted warehouses (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane) have acknowledged receipt of the RAFs. Warehouse contacts have been asked to confirm their daily receiving hours for returned goods.

**11:40 AEST –** Regulatory Officer S. Delaney noted that the ACCC has requested a copy of the proposed consumer alert text for pre-publication review. Draft sent at 11:20 AEST; response expected within two business days.
**11:30 AEDT –** Consumer Contact Lead P. Whitfield provided an update on call volumes. Between 8:30 AM and 11:00 AM today, 23 enquiries were received. Of these, 19 callers confirmed they had the affected product and were given return instructions. The remaining 4 callers were checking whether their product was affected; all were advised to check the batch number against the published list.

**13:15 AEDT –** Compliance Liaison J. Okafor reported that 3 stockists had not received the retailer notification pack due to outdated contact details. Updated email addresses obtained from the sales database. Packs resent at 12:50 AEDT. Follow-up required if no acknowledgement by Friday.

**14:00 AEDT –** Logistics Contact R. Singh confirmed that the first batch of return authorisation forms has been submitted to the Sydney warehouse. Expected first physical returns to arrive tomorrow or Thursday. Warehouse staff have been briefed on the quarantine and inspection procedure.

**15:20 AEDT –** Regulatory Officer S. Delaney submitted the revised consumer alert text to the ACCC at 15:05 AEDT. Awaiting final approval. Status: `in progress`.

**16:40 AEDT –** End of day summary. All notification activities progressing. No exceptions reported.

**Entry 004 – 13 March 2025, 09:10 AEDT**
**Subject:** Day 4 – Consumer alert approval and return logistics

**09:15 AEDT –** Regulatory Officer S. Delaney confirmed that the ACCC has approved the revised consumer alert text. The alert will be published on the Product Safety Australia website at 10:00 AM today. Status: `completed`.

**09:50 AEDT –** Consumer Contact Lead P. Whitfield reported that the recall phone line received 61 calls yesterday (12 March). Peak call period was between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM. All callers were provided with the recall details and advised to stop using the product immediately. **10:30 AEDT –** Logistics Contact R. Singh confirmed that the first physical returns have arrived at the Sydney warehouse. A total of 14 units received this morning. **11:45 AEDT –** Compliance Liaison J. Okafor noted that 2 stockists have not yet acknowledged receipt of the retailer notification pack. **13:00 AEDT –** Regulatory Officer S. Delaney advised that the consumer alert is now live on the Product Safety Australia website. A copy of the final published alert has been saved to the recall file for reference.

- Contact logs and correspondence with the three state‑based electrical safety regulators (NSW, Victoria, Queensland) confirming no further reports of incidents or injuries related to the recalled product after 15 May 2025.

- You are not required to take any further action unless new information comes to light that indicates a continuing risk associated with the product.
- Should you receive any further consumer complaints or incident reports relating to the recalled product, you are required to notify the Commission within 14 days, in accordance with section 45 of the Regulations.
- The Commission may, at its discretion, conduct a post‑recall audit within 12 months of the closure date. This audit, if undertaken, would be limited to verifying that no recalled units remain in the marketplace and that the corrective action remains effective.

**1. Consumer Refund and Reimbursement Data**

Under clause 8(2)(b) of the Recall Guidelines (Consumer Goods), you are required to provide a final statement of consumer refunds and reimbursement claims processed in connection with the recall. This statement must include, for the period 1 February 2025 to 30 June 2025:

**2. Basis for Closure**

The closure decision was made following a review of the following materials:

- Final recall outcome report (dated 20 June 2025), including statistical analysis of consumer response rates and unit recovery data.
- Certificate of destruction for 1,847 units disposed of under supervision of an authorised waste facility (see attached Annex A).
- Repair verification records for 1,236 units returned and subsequently remediated, including test certificates from an independent electrical safety laboratory (NATA-accredited).
- Copies of all consumer notifications, including the original recall advertisement published in *The Sydney Morning Herald* and *The Australian* on 14 March 2025, and the updated notification issued on 2 April 2025.
- Contact logs and correspondence with the three state‑based electrical safety regulators (NSW, Victoria, Queensland) confirming no further reports of incidents or injuries related to the recalled product after 15 May 2025.

The Commission is satisfied that the recall was conducted in accordance with the approved recall plan dated 10 March 2025, and that the company has met all obligations under the *Australian Consumer Law* and the *Consumer Product Safety (Recalls) Regulations 2024*.

**3. Administrative Notes**

Please note the following administrative matters:

- The recall file will remain open for a period of 30 days from the date of this letter for the sole purpose of receiving any late‑emerging incident reports. After that date, the file will be archived in accordance with the Commission’s records management policy.
- You are not required to take any further action unless new information comes to light that indicates a continuing risk associated with the product.
- Should you receive any further consumer complaints or incident reports relating to the recalled product, you are required to notify the Commission within 14 days, in accordance with section 45 of the Regulations.
- The Commission may, at its discretion, conduct a post‑recall audit within 12 months of the closure date. This audit, if undertaken, would be limited to verifying that no recalled units remain in the marketplace and that the corrective action remains effective.

**4. Contact**

Should you have any questions regarding this matter, please contact the undersigned at (02) 6200 0000 or by email at recalls@cpsca.gov.au. For future correspondence, please quote the file reference shown at the top of this letter.

Yours sincerely,

The Commission acknowledges receipt of that certificate and confirms that the destruction of recalled units at the Cleanaway Waste Management Facility, Unanderra, on 18 June 2025, has been accepted as satisfying the corrective action component of the recall plan.

This letter sets out the remaining reporting requirements to bring Product Recall 2025-03 to a formal close. Please note the timeframes below are calculated from the date of this letter and, where a due date falls on a weekend or a public holiday in the Australian Capital Territory, the due date is extended to the next business day.

**1. Consumer Refund and Reimbursement Data**

Under clause 8(2)(b) of the Recall Guidelines (Consumer Goods), you are required to provide a final statement of consumer refunds and reimbursement claims processed in connection with the recall. This statement must include, for the period 1 February 2025 to 30 June 2025:

- the total number of refunds issued to consumers;
- the total value of refunds issued (in Australian dollars);
- the number of claims received but not yet processed as at 30 June 2025, together with the reasons for any delay; and
- a breakdown of refunds by state or territory, where the consumer’s address is known.

The statement must be certified by your external auditor and submitted to the Commission by **24 July 2025**.

**2. Retailer and Distributor Confirmation**

You are reminded that the Commission has not yet received written confirmation from all retailers and distributors listed in your recall distribution list confirming that recalled units have been removed from sale and returned to Brightline Home Appliances Pty Ltd or destroyed. A template for this confirmation was provided in the Commission’s letter of 12 March 2025.

Please provide, by **18 July 2025**:
